clue.text: Law rests with male hospital attendants

parts.note: law and order: a law is an order laid down
rests means lies, as in lies down

explanation.surface: Statutes are said to sit alongside the men who work on hospital wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderlies are the porters and helpers on hospital wards, traditionally men.

clue.text: Stalk blown in the wind

definitions.meaning: a stem of a waterside grass
the vibrating strip in a woodwind instrument, which the player blows

explanation.definitionFit: A tall grass stem, and also the vibrating tongue in oboes and clarinets, members of the wind section.

clue.text: Some wearing down for example, around sculptor

indicators.note: around tells us the abbreviation's two letters go either side of the artist

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: A sculptor wearing down a piece of stone, set out as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' at the start adds no letters; it softens the definition 'wearing down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock that is being worn away gradually by water or wind is being eroded.

clue.text: Boy holding scheme for the country

indicators.note: holding means the boy's word wraps round the scheme's word

parts.note: a boy is a lad
a scheme is a plan

explanation.surface: A boy with a scheme for a trip to the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the region of far northern Scandinavia, home of the Sami, loosely a country.

clue.text: Slippery characters sleep around, mostly

indicators.note: around means the shortened word is turned back to front
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shady people who sleep around, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SLEEP to SLEE, and 'around' turns that into EELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are notoriously hard to hold, the image behind calling a crafty person slippery.

clue.text: Its twin-speakers shatter goblet, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A loud stereo is so powerful that it breaks a wine glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' signals the anagram of SHATTER GOBLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A big portable stereo cassette player with two built-in loudspeakers, popular in the 1980s.

clue.text: Housing assistance

definitions.meaning: lodgings or a place to live
help given by fitting in with someone's needs

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lodgings and an obliging adjustment to help someone.

clue.text: Head fuzz?

parts.note: read not as hair on the scalp but as the head of the fuzz, slang for police

explanation.definitionFit: Fuzz is slang for police, and the head of a force is its senior officer.

clue.text: A body of musicians, one at a time, in diverting manner

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union, the UK body for musicians
one at a time means singly

explanation.surface: A band whose players come on one by one, to the audience's delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverting means entertaining, so done in a diverting manner is entertainingly.

clue.text: Most advanced military units of top rank

explanation.definitionFit: The forward position facing the enemy, and figuratively anything leading or foremost.

clue.text: Second note is a tiny speck

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second
TE is the seventh note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A quick remark that a second musical note is very small.
explanation.definitionFit: A mote is a particle of dust, as in the mote in someone's eye.

clue.text: Inner pyramid ascertained as resting-place of this king

indicators.note: inner means letters inside the following words
the words are where the name lies, so the run sits within them

explanation.surface: An archaeologist establishes that the inner pyramid houses a king's tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner' and 'as resting-place of' both show the run hides in pyraMID AScertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is the legendary king of Phrygia whose touch turned things to gold.

clue.text: Expedition in direction of ancient city

parts.note: to means towards
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A journey heading for a ruined old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey made round several places, an outing or trip.

clue.text: Epitaph over Yorkshire cathedral

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the stock gravestone inscription
on means over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: Words on a tombstone above a grave in a northern cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Scottish island is non-clerical

parts.note: taken as written
lay means not of the clergy

explanation.surface: A remark that a Hebridean island has no clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is one of the Inner Hebrides, famous for its peaty whiskies.

clue.text: What activity traps family in foul air?

indicators.note: traps means the polluted air word encloses the family word

parts.note: smog is polluted air
kin means family

explanation.surface: A question: which habit leaves the whole family breathing dirty air?
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting up tobacco is the habit that fills a room with fumes the family breathes.

clue.text: Refuse the job of Eliza's father

definitions.meaning: collecting rubbish is the work of a bin man
Alfred Doolittle, father of Eliza in Shaw's Pygmalion, a rubbish collector

explanation.definitionFit: In British English this is a bin man, and Alfred Doolittle in Pygmalion worked as one.

clue.text: Horatio's ways of seizing opponents

definitions.meaning: belonging to Horatio, Admiral Lord Nelson
wrestling holds, arms locked under the opponent's armpits behind the neck

explanation.definitionFit: Possessive of the admiral's surname, and the plural of a wrestling hold.

clue.text: Sinful, having rook taken by moving castle

indicators.note: taken by means put inside the rearranged letters
moving means the castle's letters are shifted about

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess move in which a rook is captured when the castle moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges CASTLE to SCALET; 'taken by' puts R inside. In chess the rook is also called the castle, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet, as in a scarlet woman, means openly immoral.

clue.text: Caught in light shoe? It's a disgrace!

indicators.note: in means placed inside the footwear word

parts.note: a sandal is a light open shoe
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught wearing sandals is told it is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a shameful public affair that brings disgrace.

clue.text: Earring-one that may drop off

definitions.meaning: a small ring worn to stop a pierced ear closing
someone who nods off to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: A small ring keeping a piercing open, and someone who falls asleep.

clue.text: City street at the end

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city road found right at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Last means coming at the end, final.

clue.text: Infant left in the tower, here

parts.note: a babe is a baby

explanation.surface: A baby abandoned in a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of Babel in Genesis, built to reach heaven.

clue.text: Amaze with endless acrobatic feat in film

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stunt is a daring feat performed in a film

explanation.surface: A movie audience is astonished by a daring trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or stagger someone.

clue.text: Colour of money is about right

indicators.note: about means the money word goes round the other letter

parts.note: the ecu was the old European currency unit

explanation.surface: The hue of banknotes is roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Give advance notice of programme

definitions.meaning: a list of acts at a show or theatre

explanation.definitionFit: To announce an event in advance, and the list of what is on at a show.

clue.text: Our helicopter adapted for Belgian detective

indicators.note: adapted means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rotorcraft modified for a famous sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' signals the anagram of OUR HELICOPTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's moustached Belgian sleuth, hero of Murder on the Orient Express.

clue.text: The comma in lepidopterist's collection?

parts.note: not the punctuation mark but the comma as an insect pinned in a lepidopterist's display case

explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a species of winged insect with a white comma-shaped mark under its wing.
